steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Why does Anatoliy not want me to go with him?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What is he... going to do?

steps.name: Brave Servant
steps.text: It's better if you don't know.

steps.name: Brave Servant
steps.text: Please trust in the Generalik. He will not break his promise to you.

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: ...What a pain...

steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: P-Please, sir, I'm begging you! All our research is here, all of it!

steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: But that door, I don't know... I really don't know how to open it!

steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: None of us have the authorization, except Director Alita Valueva, but she...

steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: But she's dea—

steps.name: Frightened Voice
steps.text: ARGH!
At the back of the group surrounded by soldiers, Klim cannot stop himself from turning his head, looking back at the corpse tossed away in the dark corridor.
He cannot make out anything, yet still he franticly turns his head over and over, until the hilt of a soldier's sword strikes his skull.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: (Quietly) Stop that!

steps.name: Grumpy Voice
steps.text: Now, as for the rest of you...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Can anyone here tell me why not even my authority is able to work here, hmm?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Am I, perhaps, lower on the totem pole than a lowly lab director?
Silence. Nobody dares to open their mouth without thought, out of fear of the terrible fate that might pounce on them at any time.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You, in the first row, the closest to the corpse. Speak.

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: Only a small handful of high-level researchers can open that door, out of concerns for a security leak—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Which means even I am locked out of this door?

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: AIEE—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Don't kill her just yet. Tell me, where are these high-level researchers?

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: ...Th-They w-were all, you—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Oh, how unfortunate. However, since you know so much about it, then surely there must be some sort of emergency opening procedure?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: A laboratory like this must has one.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Or do you know, and simply do not wish to tell me?

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: N-No, sorry, I-I don't know, I'm just speculating based on past experience, it's my job—

steps.name: Timid Researcher
steps.text: Forgive me, Generalik, I—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Useless trash.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What a waste of time. Kill them, starting from the right-hand side. Keep going until one of them figures out a way to open this, or until they're all dead.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: What about the Marshal's orders?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mother only told me to bring me back results. She said nothing about bringing back the things underground.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: So long as I do my best, she will not blame me.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Look. Are these not the results of my hard labor...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: The great effort of enduring this headache?
He points towards the corpses and bloodstains scattered across the floor, an innocent smile upon his face.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir... Absolutely correct.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I truly don't understand what people see in this thing. If you don't supply it energy, it turns into a bomb. Why not simply blow it up ourselves and start over?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: To think it was something like this that forced Mother to abandon Zelgrad... How wretched.

a.text: That man over there, what's he saying?

steps.text: The man standing at the very back can no longer hear clearly. Those shrieks, those sounds of escape, capture, and execution, they are like an automated assembly line in a factory, occurring without his input.
He does not try to turn his head again. Instead, amidst all this noise, amidst his memories playing on loop, he sees only a glimpse of the corpse of his wife...
He falls to his knees, oblivious to the chaos around him.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Alita...

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Hey, get up!

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: I said, GET UP!
The young man raises a hand, signaling the guards to stop. A sobbing man is yanked to his feet and tossed aside. Then he walks toward the kneeling man.
The panicking, numbed crowd automatically splits to form a passage for the Generalik.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What are you saying? Why are you kneeling?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Alita...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You know this woman?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I couldn't... leave her.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Merely one of the lab's logistics staff, Generalik, in charge of sweeping and such. He's just scared.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: No, he must have some connection with that woman who allowed those people to enter the prototype core.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: He might know more than the rest. Pull him up, use your swords or whatever to break him out of his daze—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hierda? Why are you—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You didn't listen to me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It was you who broke our promise this time.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I did not!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Then how do you explain the bodies on the floor, these trembling, pitiful people... and that man kneeling by you?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You're still... You're still hurting them, and hurting yourself at the same time. When you take the lives of others so easily, you increase the weight pressing down on yourself.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I have no way... I have no way of stopping you. I can only look on helplessly as you slide towards ruin. You can no longer know salvation, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I can, I can still be saved! I just need you to be by my side—always!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Why... Why does everyone always try to coerce me like this?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mother is disappointed in me, these servants have no respect for me... They all see me as a useless monster. Are you the same?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hm... hm?
Hierda steps forward, gently holding Anatoliy's hands. He is taller than her, lankier than her. His two hands dwarf hers, far larger than the average adolescent.
She holds them, slowly tightening her grip.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I don't know what this monster you speak of actually is, but a true monster wouldn't care about how others see it. A monster's heart only has space for itself.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You are angry because others mock you, you weep because your friends leave you... You feel pain, don't you?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You are always going against your own intentions to hurt others, to the point you can't see just how much you are hurting yourself.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I believe that deep in your heart, you don't want to do this. Your reaction today proves this.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You say that everyone is coercing you.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But I believe.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You believe... you believe in me? This means you won't leave me, right?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I don't want to leave, but if you keep being like this, without the slightest hint of change, I must leave.

spans.text: I don't want to leave, but if you keep being like this, without the slightest hint of change, I

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You are so very tired. If you continue on, you will collapse. And all I can do is watch as you doom yourself to this future.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Et tu, Hierda...? Have you joined the others in refusing to save me?

spans.text: Have you joined the others in refusing to save me?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It's not that I don't want to, but I can't. I simply cannot. As I said before, I can soothe the pain in your body, but I cannot soothe the scars on your soul.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It weeps blood. Can you not feel it?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You hurt yourself because of your mother's impossible expectations, but why would a mother be this cruel to her own child?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: She has tossed you into such circumstance, forcing you to go against your own desires, to destroy a beautiful city, to end so many innocent lives.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: She pushed you in front of all her problems. Maybe she believes you can handle them, but if you never had the right to choose, then does she truly believe in you, or...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Are you just a tool to her?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Tools can be replaced, Anatoliy. But you are not a tool, or a monster, are you?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What... What should I do?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Tell me, Hierda. Tell me—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Maybe all you need to do is give her proof.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Proof that you are not a tool, but instead, a human who lives and breathes.

steps.name: Exhausted Miner
steps.text: ...We've gathered most of the people in this neighborhood, Tulin. Tonya did her best, but not everyone wanted to come.

steps.name: Exhausted Miner
steps.text: Reunion's helping us raid the sentry post. We can't afford to waste any time.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Right. Appreciated.

steps.name: Resident A
steps.text: Tonya, you said this was something important, something to do with our lives. You're not lying to us again, right?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: No, I'd never.
A crowd of people stand there, sunlight shining on their faces. Many of them look calm, glancing around in puzzlement.
The miners can no longer hold back their rage. They who have returned from the depths of hell can only see such aloofness as hate. They roll up their sleeves and clench their fists...

steps.name: Red
steps.text: It's time, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Time for?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Time for you to do what you do best: stand up and give a few inspiring words to everyone.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Red... I'm not sure if I still have the right to do that.
'Bam'—
Someone pats her on the back. Talulah turns, and is greeted by Tulin's smile. The ever-cool-headed leader steps forward, standing in front of the crowd.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: My Zelgradian friends! My name is Ivan Tulin, and these are my companions behind me.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: I am no different from the rest of you. I too am one of the many workers at the beck and call of Ursus, one who has mined in the Northern Tundra for over a decade.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: For all those years, the first thing I do every time I left the mines would be to look up at the sky, memorizing the shape of the clouds, the warmth of the sun, the sound birch leaves make when you step on them.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Every time I was deep in the darkest, most dangerous mineshafts, I only had to close my eyes, and those beautiful things would be at my side.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: But I could not do so just now.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: What I have seen was a hundred times darker than the deepest pit. Underneath your feet, somewhere you cannot see, your fellow Ursines are being brutally murdered.

steps.name: Resident A
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Some of you saw how we came from the nearby autonomous district. There, we discovered a military lab, and learned their secrets.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Have you ever wondered why Zelgrad opened its doors to those with Oripathy from the rest of Ursus, why all the Infected are being gathered in one place?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: It's because the First Army's Originium supplies have nearly run dry! They are burning the Infected like firewood, then performing evil experiments behind those stone walls!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You do not want to know how those Infected are dying, dying with such indignity—

steps.name: Resident B
steps.text: My nephew only had a mild case, but those soldiers still carted him away!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: There is still time. We are fighting against the First Army, but we must first keep you all safe.

steps.name: Resident C
steps.text: Keep us safe? From what? What are these 'evil experiments' anyway?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Their research may have led to the spreading of a mysterious disease. Some of you have already seen it for yourselves. Green pustules, spots all over the body—

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Some of you even had family who died of it... This is the First Army's unforgivable sin!

News of this strange disease causes the crowd to talk amongst themselves. They talk and they talk, taking note of their conversation partners' expressions. Some faces turn grave, others look towards Tonya.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Is this the weird disease you were talking about, Tonya?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...It is.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: The Army covered it up, taking away anyone who caught it to do research...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: But that research came at the cost of their lives!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: My youngest sister, Nina... Lots of you have seen her, some of you even cradled her...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: She caught that disease, and Doctor Nadezhda Pavlovna took her in for treatment, but she still got taken away by those evil men in army clothes... and now—

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Nina... She's gone!
As Tonya lifts the swaddling blanket above her head, the raucous crowd falls silent. Many of the residents know that piece of cloth.
They have seen Tonya carry her little sister, wrapped up in that blanket, as she walked between the factories, a blissful smile always on her face.

steps.name: Resident D
steps.text: But we really haven't seen an illness like this before...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Mark's seen it. He looked after Nina for a little while after she got sick. Where is he—

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Are you... Mark?

steps.name: Feeble Resident
steps.text: I... I shouldn't have denied you like that, Tonya. I was really, really scared...

steps.name: Feeble Resident
steps.text: But... I can't keep being scared.
He takes off his jacket as he steps forward, revealing terrifying pustules on his skin. The people around him shriek as they back away.
Tonya quickly helps support him. The man who was once her friendly neighbor is now exhausted and weak. This terrifying, debilitating disease has robbed him of most of his ability to even walk.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You have all seen this poor man.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: But what you might not have realized is—

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: If we do not act, if we instead choose to cover our ears and succumb to the apathy they feed us...

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: This misfortune could fall onto each and every one of us at any time!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: The First Army, those self-righteous liars, said the sound of cannons outside the city was to protect us. They said our missing neighbors had 'gone for treatment'...

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Lies! Utterly shameless, despicable lies, all of them! When they are not busy beating prisoners, they are busy thinking up new lies.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Their 'secret laboratory' has no doctors, only butchers. They sealed our brothers and sisters in vats, like chopped up pieces of beastmeat.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Is this the 'kindness' Ursus shows us? Are such pitiful souls the Ursines they want to see?

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Those who stand above us, those who point their spears at us, they eat the bread we bake, live in the houses we make, and now they come back to us, wanting to turn us into samples of meat for the laboratory bench...

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: So long as they require it, they will infect us with Oripathy, molding us into whatever form they see fit. It was through these means that they made us impoverished and downtrodden!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Look at the ground beneath your feet. It is rotten to the core. It has rotted and reeked for decades, centuries even.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: But now, two paths lie ahead of us.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: You can go and be fuel for those vermin, a path where you return to your 'homes', where you line up and wait to be shoveled into their furnaces and stoves, where you lie down in the graves they prepared for us.

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Or you can come with me, and leave this damned place. Yes, this path promises only bitter cold, but it is a path you can walk upon your own two feet, a path we were born to walk!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Come! We shall walk away with all our children, all our family, all our friends!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: Let them weep over the ruins, let their hollow souls feel the pain of having nothing!

steps.name: Tulin
steps.text: For the sake of all our tomorrows, come with me, and leave this tomb!
As Tulin yells out the last of the speech, the crowd breaks out into enthusiastic shouting of their own. Several familiar faces step up once more—Reunion has routed the nearby sentry post.
Tulin's gaze sweeps across Red, across Sirka, eventually stopping on the one leading them. Tulin locks eyes with Talulah, until the cheers and applause die down.
Talulah does not blink. She saw the expressions on the residents' faces as they looked towards Tulin. She had seen such faces before.
Many years ago, in another plaza, people looked to her this way, with eyes that said, 'So long as we follow Talulah, we can do anything'. Eyes brimming with hope.
Talulah smiles. A smile of relief, maybe. It is as if after countless days of wandering the endless wastes alone, she suddenly sees another pair of footprints walking alongside her.
But there is not just one pair. Countless others walk with her through the Northern Tundra.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Tulin's people are ready, Talulah. They'll be in charge of mobilizing, organizing and evacuating the residents of other districts, while we draw the army's attention, just like we planned.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: How are things on your side, Closure?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ready to head out whenever. Whatever happens, I need to get past that wall.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I'll also be heading to the wall. Anatoliy must be overseeing the research institute...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: He escaped me once through sheer luck. It won't save him a second time.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Right. Don't get too caught up in battle, Red. Protecting the residents while they evacuate is our top priority.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: ...Take care, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I still have a few things I need to say to everyone in Reunion. You can head off first.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sure. Let's go, Sirka.
The crowd slowly disperses. Talulah turns around. A red-haired Reproba sits on some steps not too far away, silently watching her.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: It's just us here now, Talulah.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Get started with your excuses already. You could've kept skulking around in the shadows, but you chose to show yourself again and stir up trouble for some reason—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I need to apologize to you, Lyudmila.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Not just to you, but to everyone from that time, to those who believed that I could bring them into the future...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Even if many of them can no longer hear me.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: So you came to Zelgrad to atone?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Atonement is beyond me. I just want to do... the things I did not do back then.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: (Quietly) ...Enough.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Are you going to go with Closure to find the Sarcophagus?
The young redhead turns her head to look at the crowd heading towards the edge of the city. The din in the background is formed from their footsteps, alongside cannon fire from who-knows-where.
She understands that there is not much time for a chat right now. Whether they want to talk about the past or the future, there are much more pressing matters when countless lives are on the line—
But she speaks all the same.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I should be investigating it thanks to some intelligence I found, but I figured something would go wrong, so I gave that info to some other people who are also looking for it.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: If my guess is right... The answer should be inside.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: It's a strange feeling. I only learned recently that there's a lot of things I don't have to take on alone.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Besides, you know how it is. If we have to fight in the alleys, my Arts can stop an entire army. My smoke can screen more people while they get out of here.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Lyudmila, what I meant was, your father once gave everything for the Sarcophagus. I'm not trying to change your mind, but if you still have regrets—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Listen, Talulah. I used to hate you, just like how I hated how powerless I was.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Lyudmila...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I hated all the lies and betrayal, until... I suddenly realized one day, all those memories that chained me, they didn't feel so heavy anymore.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Slowly but surely, I found myself with more things I have to do. Like how I should be heading off with those people over there right now.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Ivan Tulin... An amazing one.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Hmph. I've heard that name before. One who writes good essays, ones as sharp as a knife, but what Tulin's really like, that remains to be seen.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: I won't believe in perfect leaders again.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You might be right.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: So you see, we don't need to keep working together. We have our own battlefields to fight. I need to help people evac, and you...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You need to do the things you haven't done yet.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Then... I still have... one last request.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Oh? And what do you have left that affords you the privilege?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The fact that the Volnov is the closest Fourth Army unit to Zelgrad.

spans.text: is the closest Fourth Army unit to Zelgrad.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You know I've got a choice. I can choose to 'help' you declare war on the First Army, trigger some mutually assured destruction, the works.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: You would rather go down and be reunited with Lieutenant Sirka than be resigned to your fate? How touching.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Then let me hear her voice one more time.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Just one last time.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: After that, Sechin will follow your plan to the letter.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Bring her here.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I thank Your High Excellency for your kindness.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: ...Scioppa—
It is the exact same voice. The same voice he has heard reporting in over staticky comms countless times.
It is unlike the one he hears when they are together, talking face to face. Only on the battlefield, during drills, during dire circumstances when emotions are hard to read—
Does he hear this calm but cold voice.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: ...I will find you, Sirka.

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: Don't, Scioppa. Not for me.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: It's not just for you. I'm not letting any of my people get banished because of Oripathy again.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'll find all of you.

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: ...Arrogant fool.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Now, I set off.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But before that, I've got a question for you. The last words you said to me before we got—

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Enough, take her away—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: —What was it?

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I said, take her away!

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: I have satisfied your final request, Major Razin. Do not push your luck.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Yes, you have satisfied me, and I've got no further requests.

spans.text: satisfied me, and I've got no further requests.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'm just a little hurt. Seems she's forgotten them already.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: But I still remember. Her last words to me were: 'We will not meet again, not until we hear the call of death herself.'

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: What a cruel woman.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Cut the call.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Roger!

steps.name: Evgeny
steps.text: Scioppa Razin! You—

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: That actually was Sirka, Scioppa—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'm an idiot.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: That wasn't Sirka. It was never Sirka!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: It was just a war caster imitating her, using snippets from open comms as a model! How did it take me this long to notice?!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: No wonder he didn't let me take that dagger. Probably another product of Arts, unable to keep its shape...

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: The only bit I understood was you saying that wasn't Sirka. Are you a hundred percent sure?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: They analyzed how she speaks, even compiled the details of how she tried to kill herself after they arrested her for extra believability, but it was all wrong. Now that I look back, every single word was wrong.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: War casters can't read minds, so they have no idea what Sirka said to me.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Besides, our noble lady wouldn't kill herself the moment she got captured, she'd take down a bunch of them with her.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Hah. Even you saw right through it, while I only just realized. I really am a complete idiot.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Then do we stick to that old bastard's plan?

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: No... of course not.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Oleg, get everyone who can use concealment Arts up on deck right now. Use the technique I taught you to wipe the Volnov off the positioning systems for a while.

spans.text: Oleg, get everyone who can use concealment Arts up on deck right now. Use the technique I taught you to wipe the
off the positioning systems for a while.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Test all our equipment, Efim. Once the ship is concealed...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I'll give a ship-wide broadcast.

steps.name: Confused Soldier
steps.text: Huh? New orders from the boss?

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: He better not be trying to get us off the ship again! I'll hide in the boiler room if I have to—

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: All hands on the Volnov, this is Scioppa Razin.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: So formal... What's going on?

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: First, let's forget all the foolish decisions I made earlier. Once everything's been settled, you can turn around and have a good laugh at me.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: This next part of the announcement is more important, though.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: I've already transferred all command authority to Oleg Khmelnytsky, a fine fellow you all know and love.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Concerned Soldier
steps.text: Transferring command authority...

steps.name: Concerned Soldier
steps.text: Where're you going, Chief?

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: ...Ever since that annihilation operation in December, I've found myself thinking about what 'Volnik'—maybe even the 'Sechin' made up of us Volniki—actually means.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: In peace time, we're relatively privileged, looking after the land outside the cities for the tsar, but at the same time, we have to face Catastrophe, along with unending migration and separation.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: In war time, we're valiant fighters, the sharpest, nimblest blade in any army's arsenal. But we're forever outsiders, never fitting in, never allowed to die with even a little dignity.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: I often wonder, does it really have to be this way? We non-Ursus have been living and dying like this for so long, but is this actually right?

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: But now I know. It's not right. So we need to get ourselves out of this mess.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: ...To be honest, I should've realized before we wandered into the clutches of the Fourth Army.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: The past exploits of our people have already been forgotten. Even deeds as recent as our parents' generation, where they served as the vanguard for both sides of the Great Rebellion, have been lost to history, their names unrecorded.

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: And now, will we follow the same road they did, a road that ends only in the blackness of death?

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: No, no we won't.

steps.name: Diligent Soldier
steps.text: You tell 'em, boss...

steps.name: Voice on the PA
steps.text: As your chief, I should be fighting for you all. Even if all I'm fighting for is a chance to break free of our chains.

spans.text: As your chief, I should be fighting for you all. Even if all I'm fighting for is a
to break free of our chains.

steps.text: Upon the deck, inside the control center, in the boiler room, in the corners of the storeroom, countless men and women lift their heads to listen to their chieftain's speech. They silently nod, or they wait in doubt.
They feel ripples echoing across their hearts as they hear these words, even if they do not fully understand their meaning.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Sirka hasn't been captured by Evgeny Andrianov. We were all taken in by his lies.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: And the entire reason he used such a despicable scheme was to ruthlessly send us into the front lines against the First Army as cannon fodder—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Well, we're not just going to sit back and let them kill us.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Some people who are already dead said it best. Ursus is burning down, we just never saw the flames.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: The mines in the north are shut, and so are the factories in Central. Angry workers march through the streets with weapons in hand. Even students are lifting their skinny fists in resistance—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I say it's time. Time for us to ask Ursus to honor our promise.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Our ship and her crew are no longer in the 'terrorizing commoners' business.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I want us to leave the Fourth Army, leave anywhere that would treat us only as weapons.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I want freedom for the Volniki, true freedom, even if it means meeting with the Viy.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Hah...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I declare that the Volnov will not be heading towards Zelgrad. From now on, the Special Tactics Formation 'Sechin' is no longer a part of the Fourth Army.

spans.text: will not be heading towards Zelgrad. From now on, the Special Tactics Formation 'Sechin' is no longer a part of the Fourth Army.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I will personally inform Kuznetsov—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: —Who?!
Mutineering, instigation, insubordination...
You have violated martial law. You have betrayed your orders.
You all... should die.
The very next moment, space warps around Scioppa. He senses himself being dragged into a free-floating space, apart from the ship.
'Morvan'. This is clearly 'frozen space', a place that leaves the one being interrogated feeling like they are being eaten away by fire, both mentally and physically.
He knows this is only an illusion, but it also means he has to use all his mental fortitude and more to break free of it.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Kuznetsov's personal guard... The war casters.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: It's only been a few years, but I don't recognize your uniforms at all now. Did they rework how they make you people, or did Evgeny have other designs for you?
The war caster does not reply. Several streams of Arts fly towards him like arrows without the caster even raising their hand, piercing through his flesh.
His one and only warning.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Gah—!

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: Major Scioppa Razin, commander of Special Tactics Formation, Sechin.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: In the name of Marshal Evgeny Andrianov Kuznetsov of the Fourth Army, I give you your final orders.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: 'Direct your men to continue onwards. You are not permitted to rest before you reach Zelgrad.'

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: If the Volnov deviates in the slightest, or slows for even a second, all hands on deck will immediately be executed. Without exception.

spans.text: deviates in the slightest, or slows for even a second, all hands on deck will immediately be executed. Without exception.

steps.name: War Caster
steps.text: The ship will continue on to Zelgrad, carrying your corpses.
